title: I Let the Barbershop Wait-List Tablet Catch the Cousin Who Sat Next

parts.text: I tapped the wait-list tablet at 12:04 p.m. and got 14. At 12:09 a cousin of barber Dez sat in the chair with no ping. The screen said: TABLET ORDER. NO COUSINS. NO WAVES. I was thirty, fade, holding number 14. Dez waved clippers. "Family is a walk-in." I photographed the 14, the screen, and the unpinged cousin. Then I logged a wave. At 12:16 the shop owner asked why Dez's cousin was on a chair without a tablet ping. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop owner can see an unpinged cousin in Dez's chair while 14 is still waiting.

social.video_title: The barber sat a cousin ahead of the tablet list — Part 1/2
social.description: Barbershop, number 14, and a cousin in the chair. I logged the wave. Would you have photographed the screen?

parts.text: Dez called it a cleanup until the owner asked for the log. I printed the wave, the photo, and the 14. The cousin waited. Dez cleaned after pings and told the shop cleanup was always about optics. Optics is a word barbers use when a cousin exists. Wait-list now has a second line: FAMILY PINGS. I keep 14. Dez tablets. The chair finally looks like a list, not a living room. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Wave log, waiting cousin, and a second line. Was cleanup ever no ping?
